Below is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* edit that fixes the malformed Lua `if/elseif/else` in the `createComment` function.  Because that bug prevented any annotations from ever being picked up, the `hasAnnotations` flag was never set and the LaTeX-only preamble (with `\usepackage{tikz}` and the `\circled` macro) never got injected.

```javascript
### src/resources/filters/quarto-pre/code-annotation.lua
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        createComment = function(value) 
          if #commentChars == 0 then
            return value
          else if #commentChars == 1 then
            return commentChars[1] .. ' ' .. value
          else
            return commentChars[1] .. ' '.. value .. ' ' .. commentChars[2]
          end
        end
=======
        createComment = function(value) 
          if #commentChars == 0 then
            return value
          elseif #commentChars == 1 then
            return commentChars[1] .. ' ' .. value
          else
            return commentChars[1] .. ' ' .. value .. ' ' .. commentChars[2]
          end
        end
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With this change in place, annotation lines will be detected correctly, `hasAnnotations` will flip to `true`, and the Lua filter’s `Meta` block will inject both

```latex
\usepackage{tikz}
```

and

```latex
\newcommand*\circled[1]{\tikz[baseline=(char.base)]{
  \node[shape=circle,draw,inner sep=1pt] (char) {\scriptsize#1};}}
```

into the LaTeX preamble so that PDF code annotation “circles” render as expected.
